What disappointed investors was the outlook, not the quarter it just reported.** Adjusted earnings beat estimates by 7.94% [C1], down from 9.48% [C1] the prior quarter. Management projected $32.5 billion [E7] in next-quarter revenue. That was broadly in line with expectations, but investors had grown accustomed to much bigger surprises [E9]. That’s the best-supported explanation for today’s drop, though no one can know every seller’s motive.

**This report doesn’t show an AI demand collapse.** Data Center sales rose 16% [E7] from the prior quarter. The more concrete risk is profitability: manufacturing issues with the new Blackwell chip already weighed on gross margin [E8]. Whether Nvidia can turn demand into profitable shipments matters more to the longer-term thesis than today’s close.

For your decision, separate the loss from the reason you owned $NVDA. If you were counting on an earnings-day rally, that catalyst passed. If your thesis was multiyear AI demand, watch Data Center sales, Blackwell shipments and margins. Your time horizon and ability to absorb another decline matter; your entry price alone doesn’t answer the question.

This is research, not investment advice.
